paragraphs: EagleView sells aerial imagery and property data drawn from an archive the company puts at more than 3.5 billion high-resolution images. Public agencies are one audience, with the imagery aimed at tax assessment, zoning enforcement, emergency response and infrastructure planning.

The subscription imagery product refreshes annually at 2-inch resolution, with an option to upgrade. The company says its 1-inch imagery carries nine times more detail than 3-inch imagery. Captures include straight-down orthogonal views for mapping and measurement and angled oblique views of building sides. A separate archive holds more than 25 years of imagery covering 96 percent of the United States population. New content is added daily, with annual refreshes across metro areas and high-growth regions. Customers view imagery in a browser tool or pull it through API connections into GIS, CAD, CAMA or analytics systems.
The site states that 20 of the top 20 insurers rely on the company. Governments, insurers, utilities, AEC firms and environmental professionals are named as users of the imagery archive.
